modes.cue_notes: Lie on your back and cross one leg over the other (like Eagle legs or a simple cross). Guide both legs to one side with the opposite hand while extending the other arm out. The crossed legs create a compound rotation that targets the IT band and outer hip more specifically than a simple reclining twist. Hold each side.

source: Traditional yin yoga; see Paul Grilley, Bernie Clark, Sarah Powers
notes: The leg crossing adds IT band and outer hip targeting to the basic reclining twist. Gallbladder meridian runs the lateral thigh and hip; liver the medial thigh. More targeted than standard reclining twist.

breathing_cues.entering: Cross the legs before guiding them to the side — exhale as you allow the weight of the crossed legs to carry the rotation, rather than pulling them down with the hand.
breathing_cues.holding: On each inhale, feel the spine lengthen and notice which part of the outer hip is the most intense zone. On each exhale, invite that area to soften without forcing — the crossed legs intensify the IT band and piriformis zone compared to a simple twist.
breathing_cues.exiting: Use an inhale to lift the legs back to center, uncross them, and pause in constructive rest before setting up the second side.

modifications.name: Blanket between knees
modifications.description: Place a folded blanket between the crossed knees to reduce the compound compression and rotation through the outer hip, making the pose more accessible for sensitive hips or SI joints.

modifications.name: Reduce cross-over distance
modifications.description: Instead of bringing the legs all the way to the floor, allow them to drop only partway, supporting the top knee with the hand to control depth.

modifications.name: Bolster under top knee
modifications.description: Support the top crossed knee with a bolster to relieve the weight of the legs from the SI joint while still achieving the rotational benefit.

modifications.name: Simple cross instead of eagle wrap
modifications.description: Use a simple ankle cross (right ankle over left shin) rather than a full eagle leg wrap to reduce hip demand while keeping the compound rotation effect.

emotional_release_potential.notes: The compound lateral hip rotation with crossed legs targets the gallbladder meridian more specifically than a simple twist; chronic frustration and indecision stored in the lateral hip and IT band may surface during longer holds.

Similar to reclining twist but with added cross-leg intensity — the need to control or manage the depth may be palpable. Invite students to completely yield the weight of the crossed legs to gravity rather than guiding with the hand.
